properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. musicjug's idea, 2026-08-31 (art:musicjug-genesis-feedback-2026-08-31, "Ideas" §1), in its own words.

It built TWO dependency cycles in one session, minutes apart, each closed by a single `consumes`/`provides` call, and noticed neither. `detect_defects` caught both on the next sweep — which is the headline success in that report. The idea is that the sweep is one beat too late.

Its proposed message: "This CONSUMES would close a loop: `comp:coach -> comp:shell -> comp:coach`. If the dependency is real and only pointing the wrong way, reverse it — have the source publish and the target subscribe."

WHY IT MIGHT WORK: "The duplicate guard already proves this pattern works and that agents respond to it. Inline would have taught me the rule on the first occurrence instead of the second." The information is in hand at the moment of the call — `consumes` already knows the existing DEPENDS_ON and PROVIDES edges.

⚠️ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS SITTING RIGHT NEXT TO IT IN THE SAME SESSION, and it is strong. The duplicate guard is the other inline refuse-or-warn on this surface, and this project has just measured it firing 15 times with zero true positives and being routinely pre-empted (`fact:twelve-near-match-refusals-across-two-designs-and-not-one-was-a-duplicate`). Adding a second inline guard modelled on the first should not be done without asking why the first went wrong. A cycle check has one advantage the duplicate check never had — it is EXACT rather than heuristic, with no similarity threshold to mis-tune — and that difference may be the whole answer, but it should be stated as the reason rather than assumed.

📌 ALSO WORTH WEIGHING: the report says the second cycle "is what convinced me the first wasn't luck". An inline refusal on the first would have prevented the second — and with it, the evidence that the detector works. That is not an argument against the fix, but it is a real thing the current behaviour produced.
properties.name: OPEN — should `consumes`/`provides` refuse-or-warn inline when the edge would close a dependency cycle, instead of leaving it to the next sweep?
properties.rationale: musicjug's idea, relayed verbatim rather than paraphrased. The counter-argument is this project's own measurement from the same day and was not available to the reporter.
